external_spec_note: The bound (toMint < baseSupply, i.e. the performance-fee mint must stay below the pre-existing supply) follows from pure in-source arithmetic over baseSupply and minLpPriceFactor's same-function derivation (two nested loops plus one state-variable snapshot); no protocol/business convention beyond the local source and language semantics is needed to justify or instantiate it.
extraction_note: Attachment point: the `uint256 toMint = (baseSupply * minLpPriceFactor) / CommonLibrary.DENOMINATOR;` statement inside the performanceFee>0 block at (contracted) line 85 -- the third, independently-scoped local named `toMint` in the function; the earlier managementFee-/protocolFee-block `toMint`s are irrelevant to this relation and excluded. Backward slice from toMint/baseSupply, within the function only: baseSupply's definition chain (L29/30/31/32/33), the baseTvls-computation loop (L44-49, needed because minLpPriceFactor's derivation reads baseTvls[i]), the hwms state-var snapshot (L66), and the minLpPriceFactor loop (L68-75, merging the `if(lpPrice>hwm){...}else{return;}` at L72-78 into one control-gate entry) -- 20 relevant statements total, transitively tracing minLpPriceFactor and baseTvls as operands of the target statement's RHS even though neither appears literally in the annotation text, per the operand-tracing precedent already established for web3bugs_42_H_01's capped-`_amount` blocks. Excluded three pure reachability gates as not redefining any relation-relevant value: `if (elapsed < ...) return;` (L25-26), `if (baseSupply == 0) {...; return;}` (L37-38), and `if (performanceFee > 0) {...}` (L67) -- none of these reassign baseSupply/minLpPriceFactor/toMint, they only gate which code path executes. Because of this, the whole `vg`/`strategyParams`/`ILpIssuerGovernance` call chain (vg.delayedStrategyParams(thisNft) etc.) and `_mint` are NOT load-bearing for this specific relation -- they feed the excluded performanceFee gate and the unrelated `treasury` argument, not toMint's own arithmetic -- hence additional_functions_n=0 and additional_contracts_n=0, a genuine feature of this relation's narrow scope (most of the function's cross-contract-governance surface is simply irrelevant to this particular bound), not an oversight. CommonLibrary.PRICE_DENOMINATOR/DENOMINATOR are counted as 2 'global' unique program values (they appear directly in counted statements, including the target statement itself) rather than filed as a Step-2 generic-library case note: they are bare named constants with no function-call/behavioral guarantee to reason about (Step 1/Step 2's load-bearing-library test in README Sec.6 targets functions/libraries with actual logic -- rounding mode, overflow-revert-vs-wrap -- not scalar constants, which fit the ordinary Unique Values accounting the same way a referenced state variable does); flagging this as a judgment call since an earlier draft of this same case's extraction (already present at this path before this pass) instead filed CommonLibrary.DENOMINATOR only as a case note with 'global:0'. CORRECTION of that earlier draft's Value/Algorithm classification: it argued the reported defect was actually the `else { return; }` control-flow statement (line 74/77-78) prematurely terminating the function rather than skipping just one token, and classified Value-level on that basis. This is contradicted by direct re-verification against the authoritative source, Web3Bugs/reports/58.md's H-02 section ('Wrong implementation of performanceFee...', https://github.com/code-423n4/2021-12-mellow-findings/issues/91): the report cites exactly the `toMint` formula (contract lines 269-271) as the wrong code, and its recommended fix changes only that line, to `(baseSupply * (minLpPriceFactor - CommonLibrary.DENOMINATOR) * performanceFee / CommonLibrary.DENOMINATOR) / CommonLibrary.DENOMINATOR` -- i.e. the deployed code omits two entire computational steps present in the fix (subtracting the DENOMINATOR growth baseline, and scaling by the performanceFee fraction, which is already computed in-scope at L65 but never used in the toMint formula at all). Per README Sec.5's classification test ('if an entire distinct processing step... is missing... that's Algorithm-level'), this is Algorithm-level, not Value-level -- reclassified accordingly in this pass. This also matches the older (non-authoritative, background-only) evaluation/RQ1/annotation_plans.md entry for this case, which independently states the same correct formula and identifies the missing performanceFee multiplication as the defect.
